evidence: src/domain/order/OrderStatus.ts: canTransition, FULFILMENT_SEQUENCE and CANCELLABLE_STATUSES are the only place the transition rules are defined
src/domain/order/Order.ts: pay/pack/ship/deliver/cancel all call the private transitionTo, which calls canTransition, so the rule is not duplicated
src/domain/order/OrderLine.ts: lineTotal is the only place a line total is calculated; Order.total adds up line.lineTotal with Money.zero()/add
src/domain/order/Order.ts: Order.place is the only place the customer, non-empty lines and unique product checks are enforced
src/domain/order/OrderRepository.ts: findById/findAll/findByStatus/save use only the module's Order and OrderStatus types
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module is one coherent unit: the Order aggregate. Order.ts is the aggregate root. OrderLine.ts is its value-like line item. OrderStatus.ts holds the status type and its state machine. OrderRepository.ts is the persistence port for the aggregate. Each invariant lives in exactly one place. Status-transition rules exist only in OrderStatus.ts (FULFILMENT_SEQUENCE, CANCELLABLE_STATUSES, canTransition), and Order defers to them through its private transitionTo method instead of copying them. Line totals are calculated only in OrderLine.lineTotal, and Order.total adds those up with Money. The rules that an order needs a customer, at least one line, and each product only once appear only in Order.place. The repository port works only in terms of the module's own Order and OrderStatus types. Order.restore rebuilds an order from saved data without re-running the checks in place. That is a normal way to reload stored data, not a bypass of the module's abstractions. No unrelated concerns, duplicated rules or bypasses were found.
